questions.q: A regional manager wants a weekly list of open opportunities over a certain size, grouped by owner. What is the best recommendation?
options: Build a CRM Analytics app with a custom recipe
A native Salesforce report or dashboard, because it is simple and reads live data
Stand up a new Data 360 identity resolution ruleset
Migrate the org to Tableau Next first
questions.explain: For a simple operational list on one object, native reports are the simplest tool that works. A more powerful platform adds cost without benefit.

questions.q: Which need is a typical sweet spot for CRM Analytics?
options: Printing a contact list
Resetting a user's password
Configuring a validation rule
Blending Salesforce data with external data and letting users explore it interactively at volume
questions.explain: Large volumes, blending external data, preparation, and deep interactive exploration are core CRM Analytics strengths.

questions.q: Twenty teams need one agreed definition of Revenue that also feeds AI assistants. Which approach does the lesson point to?
options: A governed semantic model in Tableau Next on Data 360 data
Twenty separate workbooks, each defining Revenue locally
A spreadsheet emailed weekly
A native report per team
questions.explain: A shared semantic model defines metrics once, which is the design Salesforce is building Tableau Next around.

questions.q: A company already has a mature Tableau Cloud estate over a warehouse. What does the lesson recommend?
options: Immediately migrate everything to Tableau Next
Delete Tableau Cloud
Keep building in Tableau and connect Salesforce data into it, rather than migrating only because a newer product exists
Stop using dashboards
questions.explain: Existing investment and skills are legitimate factors. Newer is not automatically better for your situation.

questions.q: Which is one of the common mistakes named in this lesson?
options: Asking who will govern the metrics
Checking licensing before designing
Starting with the simplest tool that works
Choosing the newest tool by default
questions.explain: Choosing by default, whether newest or most familiar, skips the analysis. Ignoring the cost of maintaining two platforms is another named mistake.
